extraction.name: CADS : A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography
extraction.description: CADS is an open-source framework for whole-body CT segmentation, comprising a large-scale dataset of 22,022 CT volumes with annotations for 167 anatomical structures and a segmentation model suite. It addresses limitations in existing datasets by integrating heterogeneous cross-institutional and cross-vendor data sources, enabling robust clinical deployment through comprehensive training data.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset aggregates 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources, including public archives (e.g., TCIA, TotalSegmentator), medical imaging challenges (via Grand Challenge and MICCAI), and newly contributed hospital data. Data collection involves systematic integration, standardization, and labeling of heterogeneous cross-institutional and cross-vendor data sources.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Experiments, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 4,695 (21%) of the 22,022 CT volumes contain partial annotations from public sources; the remaining 79% lack any manual annotations initially.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data includes CT scans from public archives (e.g., TCIA, TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K), medical imaging challenges (e.g., Grand Challenge, MICCAI), and newly contributed images (484 head CTs and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans). Data spans over 100 imaging facilities across 16 countries.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Pseudo-labeling is used to generate annotations for unlabeled scans through a multi-stage process involving specialized models, shape-based quality control, and multi-strategy label optimization. Missing data in annotations is addressed via this semi-supervised approach.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data is standardized by reorienting to RAS convention, resampling to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and simplifying affine transformation matrices. Facial regions in new head CTs are blurred with a Gaussian filter for privacy.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing includes reorientation to RAS, resampling to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, removal of rotation and translation components from affine matrices, and facial blurring for privacy. Images are scaled from the 5th to 95th percentiles to [0,1] and clipped for contrast enhancement.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are created using a multi-stage pseudo-labeling pipeline: initial training of specialized models on annotated data, whole-body pseudo-label generation, shape-based quality control to filter unreliable labels, and multi-strategy label optimization combining three model flavors (GT, Pseudo, Shape). Manual annotations are contributed by in-house medical teams for specific structures.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: nnU-Net framework, 3D Slicer, ANTS for non-rigid transformation, SimNIBS MRI atlas for registration, and custom tools for pseudo-labeling and quality control.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality is ensured through shape-based outlier detection using neural implicit functions, statistical ranking of model flavors based on Dice and HD95 metrics, and expert review to correct inaccuracies in existing datasets (e.g., ribs and vertebrae).
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Varies by structure; for example, some structures have annotations in over 10,000 scans, while others (e.g., buccal mucosa) appear in less than 1,000 scans with only 30 ground-truth annotations.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are created by a combination of automated methods, in-house medical research assistants, and a radiation oncologist. Specific demographics of human annotators are not provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net, vesselFM for tubular structure detection, neural implicit functions for shape-based quality control, ANTS for registration, and custom Python libraries (e.g., TPTBox).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and models are released publicly on Hugging Face and GitHub. Maintenance involves community and institutional support, but specific versioning, updating timeframe, or deprecation policies are not detailed.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Facial features are anonymized in new head CT scans using Gaussian blurring. The dataset includes data from diverse populations across 16 countries, but specific sensitive attributes (e.g., age, gender) are not detailed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The framework aims to advance robust AI solutions in radiology, making comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers. It supports clinical applications like radiation therapy planning, diagnosis, and large-scale population studies, potentially improving healthcare outcomes.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset captures clinical variability across diverse settings, but biases may arise from geographic distribution (16 countries, over 100 centers), imaging protocols, and pathological conditions. The paper notes challenges like class imbalance and potential overfitting risks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include: exclusion of pathological cases in shape-based quality control may limit learning of edge scenarios; coverage is from head to knees, excluding hands and feet; some structures require refinement (e.g., brain mask, optic chiasm, heart segmentation); facial anonymization limits detailed facial analysis; and modular design may not be as efficient as unified architectures.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for whole-body CT segmentation models. Use cases include radiation therapy planning, diagnostic radiology, anatomical landmark detection, cross-modality registration, and large-scale research studies. Usage guidelines emphasize compliance with source dataset licenses.
